product.name: ModelSpec
product.eyebrow: A language and compiler for trainable tensor programs · M0
promise: The compiler decides how it runs.
product.lede: Write the model, the loss and the optimizer in one .mspec file. ModelSpec checks every name, type and shape before anything runs, lowers the file to a typed tensor IR, derives the gradients, adds the optimizer step and trains the whole step on a CPU reference interpreter. The Vulkan backend for GPU training is the next milestone and is not built yet. No Python, PyTorch or CUDA.
product.meta: One Rust binary · CPU reference training · Vulkan planned · Apache-2.0

art.caption: The repository's example checked and trained on the CPU reference, then refused on Vulkan. Recorded by modelspec-docs from the modelspec command line, not typed.

sections.title: Errors before anything runs.
sections.lede: A shape mismatch is a compile error with both operand types, not an exception halfway through training.

items.title: Shapes in the types
items.description: Every tensor is Tensor<f32, [dims]>. matmul, add, mse and the other operators check their operands' shapes, and a mismatch names both types and the dimension it expected.

items.title: The training step is compiled
items.description: Forward pass, loss, reverse-mode gradients and the SGD update are one verified Training IR program, printed by modelspec ir --stage training.

items.title: Reproducible from the seed
items.description: Parameters and synthetic data are drawn from the train block's seed and each parameter's canonical path. Two runs with the same seed print identical bytes.

items.title: A stable code for every diagnostic
items.description: Each refusal starts with a code such as E-TYPE-012, declared next to the stage that emits it and listed with its meaning in the reference.

items.title: Gradients checked against finite differences
items.description: Every gradient rule of the operator registry is tested against central finite differences in f64 on the CPU reference.

items.title: GPU training through Vulkan and SPIR-V
items.description: Generated SPIR-V kernels on an RTX 3090 through the system Vulkan loader, checked against the CPU reference. M1; not built.

sections.eyebrow: One file to a trained model
sections.title: Parse, check, lower, differentiate, train.
sections.lede: Each stage hands a verified value to the next. The CPU interpreter runs the same Training IR a GPU backend will.
